item.title: GDP growth likely to ease to 5-quarter low of 7.5% in July-September: Icra
item.description: India's GDP growth is estimated to slow to a five-quarter low of 7.5 per cent in July-September FY27 amid external headwinds and sub-par monsoon, rating agency ICRA said on Tuesday. The Indian economy had grown at 7.8 per cent in the first quarter (April-June) of FY27 and at 8.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2025-26 fiscal year. "The slowdown (in Q2) is expected to be mild but broad-based, led by agricultural, industrial and services sectors," ICRA said in a statement. Overall, ICRA projects the GDP growth to ease slightly to 7.5 per cent in Q2 2026-27 from 7.8 per cent in Q1 2026-27, exceeding the Monetary Policy Committee's forecast of 7.2 per cent for the quarter. ICRA estimates the farm sector to clock 0.2 per cent growth in Q2, as against 3.6 per cent in Q1 FY27. Industrial sector growth is seen at 7.2 per cent against 7.7 per cent, while the services sector is estimated at 9.1 per cent against 10 per cent. item.title: India's investments in US treasuries up $38.4 billion in June-August
item.description: India's investment in US Treasury securities increased USD 38.4 billion, or 21 per cent, between June and August, coinciding with substantial inflows of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) (B) deposits into the Indian banking system. According to data compiled by PTI from the US Department of the Treasury, India's investment in US Treasuries rose to USD 219.7 billion in August 2026 from USD 181.3 billion in May 2026, just before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the concessional facility. Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank, said the RBI's foreign exchange reserves increased during the period of FCNR(B) inflows, with a portion of the accretion being invested in US Treasury securities. The RBI had introduced a special USD-INR swap facility on June 8, 2026, to encourage foreign currency inflows and strengthen the country's balance of payments position.
